extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Times and the general public (including contractors, victuallers, naval suppliers, and literary/theatre audiences)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and commentary about a newspaper's head (title-page) and principal section 'heads', plus procedural public notices (tendering, bills, pensions) published in a newspaper. Covers what makes a good head, how sections should be organised and staffed, and administrative requirements announced to contractors and claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-chosen head (newspaper title/headline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The utility of 'a well-chofen furnamc' — placing a striking title-page before a book, or an inviting Head on the front page of a newspaper, attracts readers and influences public reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A head should invite and attract the eye; a well-drawn title-page or head can powerfully recommend a paper (even promoting attention to folly or vice). Heads should be tasteful rather than imposing: 'we flatter ourselves the Heads of The Times will not be found deficient in [attraction], but by putting a meto[sic] face on affairs, will be admired for the light of its entertainments wherever it appears.' Avoid heads that are merely imposing or ostentatious (they may be 'pelted without mercy').

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal/leading section heads
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper's principal or leading heads are enumerated as: The Literary, Political, Commercial, Philosophical, Treatises, Fashionable, Humourous, News, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each head (section) should be provided with appropriate material and should appear as occasion requires. Sections will 'however always appear at the same time, but casually, at public or private affairs and call theos forth.' The choice of heads defines the paper's scope and must reflect the variety of content readers expect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section staffing and competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the heads 'are supplied with a competent share of intellects for the pursuit of their several functions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections should be staffed by contributors competent in the relevant sphere (literary critics for Literary head, legal/reporting experts for Parliamentary head, merchants for Commercial head, etc.). The paper claims such endowment is essential and not always found even among heads of State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: On parliamentary communications: 'To this great National object The Times will be most seduloufly accurate, most accurately correct, and strictly impartial in its reports.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parliamentary/official reporting should be careful, accurate and 'highly impartial' — the paper promises sedulous accuracy and impartiality in its parliamentary head. This sets an editorial standard for national/political reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and tone of a Head (avoid imposing authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: A head should not be designed 'to impose'; rather, it should attract without overbearing: 'authority sufficient to justify us in assuming a new head, with a Hea[f]er of features, but not with a design to impose.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices for the head should favour persuasion and attraction over forceful imposition. The piece cites Locke as evidence that tasteful titles can overcome resistance; the head's 'light' of entertainment is a virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatrical criticism criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards used in theatrical notices: evaluate acting quality, fidelity to character, novelty/occasion and its influence on attendance, and the degree to which performance elicits applause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: praise for 'admirable acting' and 'noble delineation of that difficult character' (Mrs. Ward as Queen) as marks of merit; comment that excellent tragedies, if not overused, would draw more attendance; note imperfections (e.g., Ryder's Falstaff 'not perfection, is yet respectable') and positive features (addresses to the gang, humour in description). Criticism attends both to artistic execution and to public reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tender submission requirements (Victualling/Navy contracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tenders must be delivered sealed, in writing (sealed up), and will be received up to a specific hour on a specified day (no regard will be had to any tender not delivered to the Board before one o'clock on the said day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions of the contract may be read at the Secretary's Office. No tender will be considered unless delivered before the stated hour; the person who makes the tender or an agent on their behalf must attend to answer when called; tenders sent by letter/after the deadline or without a responsible attendant will be disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance/answering requirement for tenders
rubrics_metrics.description: When tenders are opened/considered, the person making the tender, or some person on their behalf, must attend to answer when called; otherwise the tender will not be regarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is repeatedly emphasised for victualling and Gibraltar supply tenders: absence of the tenderer or their agent when called is grounds for ignoring the tender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bills payment and identification requirements (Navy Office)
rubrics_metrics.description: All bills registered in the course of the Navy for certain months are ordered to be paid, and persons who are possessed of the same must bring them to the Office to be assigned for payment; holders must subscribe their names and place of abode at the bottom of each bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holders of registered bills must present them to be assigned for payment and must provide identifying information (name and address) on each bill to facilitate payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chelsea Hospital pension eligibility and affidavit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons applying for Chelsea Hospital pensions must be mustered, make an affidavit of their service and age (e.g., that they are aged about a certain number of years), and magistrates will examine and take oaths regarding the claimant's status; Commissioners require satisfaction that claimants passed examinations and were discharged from their regiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must appear before Justices of the Peace in their neighbourhood, take oaths about age and service, and produce required affidavits and papers so that Commissioners of the Hospital may be satisfied. Affidavits must not omit regiments served and other material facts; false or incomplete affidavits are to be guarded against.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security concerns for shared lottery tickets
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the current Act the Office Keeper may take away the ticket (deposited in the hands of the Commissioners) three days after the old ticket is drawn, which makes sharing insecure because purchasers who share a ticket may be deprived of remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposal is made to amend the Act regulating the sharing of lottery tickets to increase the security of those who purchase shares. The page outlines the problem (Office Keeper's power to take away the ticket) and calls for public consideration of an amendment to better secure purchasers' interests.
